title: Sliding-window queue tuner and attention compactifier for continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Improve continuous batching stability and tail-latency by introducing a sliding-window queue tuner that dynamically adjusts admission thresholds and by compactifying attention hints shared across prefills. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 tail spikes for mixed-length traffic while preserving median latency and throughput. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf validation, and gated rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency reduced by >= 15% and p99 latency reduced by >= 20% on the mixed-length internal benchmark (traffic-mix-v2)
Median latency regression < 5% versus current baseline
No increase >3% in token cost per request across a 24h soak on dedicated test cluster
All new components covered by unit tests and integration tests; e2e synthetic traffic test added to CI
tasks: Spike: implement prototype sliding-window admission tuner (Diego)
Prototype: build attention-compactifier to dedupe attention metadata across concurrent prefill requests (Priya)
Bench: run mixed-length benchmark and synthetic tail workloads (SLO team)
PR: submit runtime changes with feature flag and performance counters (Diego)
QA: run 24h soak on dedicated dev cluster and collect token/cost metrics (QA)
Rollout: canary to 5% traffic, monitor trace sampling and tail latencies, then widen
comments: 2026-02-28 - Ava Chen: Kickoff. We observed recurring p99 spikes when small bursty requests arrive during long-prefill decodes. Hypothesis: static admission thresholds misalign with windowed token-rate variability.

2026-03-03 - Diego Martinez: Spike done. Sliding window (500ms buckets over 3s) adapts admission by integrating recent slot occupancy and kernel-fit hints. Early runs show p95 down 12% and p99 down 18% on toy cluster but CPU jitter increased ~2%.

2026-03-06 - Priya Kapoor: Attention compactifier prototype reduces duplicated KV-hint payloads by aggregating identical prefill prefixes across queued requests. Memory overhead +1.5% but reduces kernel mismatch rate in profiler.

2026-03-09 - SLO team: Added benchmark run with traffic-mix-v2. Sliding tuner + compactifier combined: p95 -16%, p99 -23%; median +2% (within target). Observed one regression in very-high-concurrency tiny-request workload — investigating fairness across tenants.

2026-03-12 - Diego Martinez: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8123 with feature flag runtime.feature.sliding_tuner. Includes telemetry: admission_rate, window_fill, compactify_dedupe_count. Requesting review from runtime + infra.
2026-03-14 - Security: quick review complete; no new external network surfaces. Marking security_review_required=false in ticket metadata.
2026-03-14 - Diego Martinez: Plan to canary 5% on dev-dedicated and snapshot traces. If canary stable for 48h, widen to 25% then 100% in next cycle.
decisions: Use sliding-window of 3s with 6 sub-buckets (500ms) as default; expose config for tenant overrides
Admission function will be additive combination of recent occupancy and predicted kernel-fit score (weighted 0.7 occupancy, 0.3 kernel-fit)
Attention compactifier will run opportunistically only when queued-prefill-prefix similarity > 40% to limit CPU overhead
Feature gated behind runtime.feature.sliding_tuner for safe rollout
rollout_plan: Merge behind flag to main after review
Canary 5% on dev-dedicated for 48h with extended trace sampling
If stable, widen to 25% for 72h and run full soak and cost analysis
If metrics hold, enable for all non-production clusters, then schedule enterprise release windows for Dedicated clusters
test_plan: Unit tests for sliding window math and admission controller edge cases
Integration test: inject synthetic bursty traffic and assert admission decisions do not starve long-prefills
E2E canary with traffic-mix-v2 and extended sampling (500k requests)
Chaos test: simulate 30% variance in kernel-fit predictions and verify no >10% oscillation in throughput
risks: Over-aggressive admission may increase rejection rates and degrade throughput for high-priority tenants
Compactifier CPU overhead could regress tail under extreme concurrency patterns
Telemetry volume increases; ensure sampling and aggregation to avoid backend overload
